programs.title: Governing AI at Work: A Democratic Simulation at the Grotto
outcomes: Explain the 'agents operate, people govern' model and name the human-reserved DAO actions
Draft and debate a proposal in the Proposal Forum format
Identify which workplace decisions should never be delegated to AI agents

sessions.activity: Study the Curable.X charter and mission; map which powers stay human-only and why member control matters.
Small groups draft a workplace AI-use proposal; agents (facilitators) never enact—members debate and vote.
Route tasks to working groups via the Task Router model; practice coordination between decision cycles.
Compare evidence summaries on AI in the workplace; critique how the Evidence Monitor frames findings.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized pre/post survey scores on AI governance understanding and anonymized proposal vote outcomes, contributed to shared learning models.
programs.consent: Voluntary opt-in with written explanation of data use; union stewards briefed; no personal identifiers collected; withdrawal anytime.

programs.title: Hope and Healing Waters: Lourdes as a Case in Evidence and Care
outcomes: Locate Lourdes, the Gave river and the Massabielle Grotto and describe the river-valley setting
Distinguish hope, testimony and scientific evidence using the Research Synthesis Lab method
Practice human-only decision-making in a mock Proposal Forum vote

sessions.activity: Learn how the Evidence Monitor summarizes claims; sort Lourdes cure testimonies into hope, story and evidence categories.
Discuss the charter's mission of sharing AI benefits widely; define one measurable outcome for a class project.
Students draft proposals for a school kindness project; agents draft, students debate and cast the final vote.
Track the class project against its measurable outcome using the Progress Tracker's simple dashboard.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized, aggregated quiz scores and category-sorting exercise results contributed to shared civics-of-AI learning models.
programs.consent: Guardian/parent signed consent required before any data contribution; only aggregated, anonymized classroom data shared; opt-out always available.

programs.title: Agent-Managed, Human-Governed: NGO Field Playbook
outcomes: Adapt the six-agent DAO workflow to an NGO program cycle
Design measurable charter outcomes and track them honestly
Draft proposals and grants with agent support while keeping enactment human

sessions.activity: Translate the Curable.X charter into an NGO theory of change with 2-3 measurable outcomes.
Simulate the Collaborator Scout and Task Router: map partners, route tasks, form working groups.
Use the Proposal & Grant Drafter pattern: agents draft, staff review, leadership enacts—never the reverse.
Build a progress-tracking template against charter outcomes and practice reporting gaps candidly.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized outcome-indicator templates and program-cycle timelines, stripped of beneficiary and org identifiers, for shared NGO playbooks.
programs.consent: Organizational data-sharing agreement; participant opt-in; beneficiary data never shared; anonymization reviewed before contribution.

programs.title: Curable Cell Startup: Launching a Nonprofit Learning Circle
outcomes: Understand the W3 LLC Series 4 structure and steward roles
Run a decision cycle where agents draft and humans vote
Connect the Lourdes setting's theme of hoped-for cures to ethical communication about outcomes

sessions.activity: Board-style walkthrough of the charter, reserved human powers (final vote, amendments, treasury, appointments).
Practice evidence-summarization on a nonprofit topic; discuss honest framing versus overclaiming 'cures'.
Volunteers draft, board debates, humans cast the final vote on a small pilot proposal—agents never enact.
Set up progress tracking for the pilot and schedule the next human decision cycle.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized decision-cycle metrics (turnout, proposal counts) and de-identified training feedback for shared governance models.
programs.consent: Written opt-in for individuals; board approval for organizational data; personal identifiers removed; participants may withdraw contributions at any time.
